A Texas school district is going all-in on iPads and MacBook Neo as part of a new $11 million deal. The Beaumont Independent School District is phasing out its fleet of Chromebook laptops in favor of Apple products, citing better stability, lower cost, and improved performance.

The Beaumont Independent School District board has approved a four-year, $11.19 million lease agreement to upgrade its technology ecosystem, according to the Beaumont Enterprise this week.

As part of the deal, the district will provide 14,585 Apple devices to students and staff from pre-K through 12th grade. The new batch of Apple products will replace Chromebooks that have been in use for years—many purchased more than five years ago. The district had been spending nearly $500,000 annually to repair and support the Chromebook laptops.

The new plan includes more than 4,000 iPads for pre-K through 2nd grade students, along with 9,500 MacBook Neo units for 3rd through 12th grade students. The district is also setting aside 1,000 MacBook Neo units for teachers.

The district compared the MacBook Neo against offerings from Lenovo and Asus, ultimately determining that the MacBook Neo "had the strongest performance and stability among the devices evaluated." Apple's more favorable financing terms, along with access to AppleCare services, also factored into the decision.
